one_month_reasoning: The window to 2026-11-01 very likely contains Q3 FY26 results. FormFactor has reported on a Wednesday every quarter (2024-10-30, 2025-10-29, 2026-04-29, 2026-07-29), so the likely date is Wed 2026-10-28; the 'Nov 4' calendar entry is last year's 10-Q filing date (supervisor finding, consistent with my round-1 date pattern). The date is not announced yet: EDGAR shows no 8-K since the Q2 release, only Forms 4 and 144 through Sep 17. A beat against the $270M / $0.86 guide is likely. But the 10-Q confirms that $7-9M of IEEPA tariff refunds land in Q3, so the Q4 guide will lose about 300bp of one-off margin and take on start-up costs from Farmers Branch, where the 10-Q says production begins late in Q4 FY26. That makes a soft-looking Q4 margin guide a real risk just after the stock ran from about $92 (early-Sep low) to $149 on one sell-side note. Momentum and post-earnings drift point the other way, so I stay neutral. The distribution is centred at about $148.5, between the brief's $147.90 and the $149.15 Twelve Data close, with lognormal sigma of 21% for the month (85% annual / 3.5 = 24%, trimmed because part of the realized vol came from one-off re-rating jumps). The 1-month ladder barely changes from round 1.

fair_value.method: A blend of forward P/E and EV/sales. Forward P/E: clean NTM non-GAAP EPS at Oct-2027 of about $4.30 x 30x = $129, plus about $5/share of net cash = $134, weight 0.7. EV/sales: forward revenue of about $1.30B x 7x plus about $0.40B projected net cash, over about 80M diluted shares = $119, weight 0.3. Result: about $130, roughly 12% below spot.

In-lane base rate for FORM's own multiple at peak margins. At the Apr-2021 weekly peak of about $50.85, FORM traded at 32x FY21 non-GAAP EPS of $1.59 (FY21 was a record year, GM about 47%). The current price implies about 10-11x run-rate sales, a record for FORM. Its 2021 and 2024 peaks implied about 4.5-6x (about $50-62 on $0.77B and $0.76B of revenue with about 77-78M shares). 7x credits structurally higher margins and the AI mix.

bear.story: A semi-test cycle rollover: HBM/DRAM capex digestion (SK hynix was 24.3% of Q2 revenue), share loss to Technoprobe, or an AI capex pause. Clean EPS stalls near $3.0 and the multiple derates toward 20-22x. FORM has fallen about 61% peak-to-trough twice on weekly closes ($50.85 to $19.19 in 2021-22; $61.99 to $24.17 in 2024-25), and 49% within 2026 itself. A 60% fall from the $160 high would be $64.

base.story: Growth continues: clean NTM EPS of about $4.3 at about 30-32x plus cash. EPS grows about 35%, but the multiple compresses from about 48x clean run rate, so the price ends roughly flat to slightly down.

bull.story: The Nvidia/TSMC second-source ramp shows up in reported numbers (Nvidia back above 10% of revenue), HBM4 test intensity rises, and Farmers Branch lifts margins above 55%. EPS reaches about $5.3 and the stock holds a 40x+ momentum multiple.

thesis_break_reason: $88 is about 41% below the $149 close, below the early-September low of about $92, and about 20x clean NTM EPS of $4.30, the bottom of FORM's non-trough multiple range. Trading there would most likely mean a fundamental break rather than ordinary volatility: an HBM/DRAM order cut, visible share loss to Technoprobe, a failed Nvidia second-source ramp, or gross margin settling below the roughly 51% underlying level once the tariff refunds roll off and Farmers Branch costs hit COGS.

reasoning: Round 2 revisions follow the supervisor's findings, which I verified where they mattered. (1) Clean earnings: I fetched the Q2 FY26 10-Q, which confirms the IEEPA tariff-refund disclosure under Recent Developments. The supervisor puts the one-offs at about 300bp of the 54% Q3 GM guide, so the clean run rate is about $0.77/quarter. I lowered NTM EPS at Oct-2027 from $4.50 to $4.30. (2) Multiple base rate, my lane: I checked FORM's own multiple at past peaks. In Apr-2021 it was 32x FY21 non-GAAP EPS of $1.59 in a record-margin year. At the Oct-2022 trough it was about 13-14x. The Jul-2024 peak was about 54x FY24 EPS of $1.15, but on depressed margins, and a 61% fall followed. I agree with the supervisor that the 36x five-year average is inflated by trough years, and I cut the multiple from 32x to 30x. (3) Drawdowns: on weekly closes they were about 61%, not 55%, and the 2026 June-July swing was -49%. I lowered the bear price from $70 to $65 and kept a fat left tail (P(<$59) = 10%). (4) The Deutsche Bank Nvidia thesis is one sell-side original, so I moved it from the base EPS path to the bull case. The 10-Q does show Nvidia as a 10.2% customer in Q1. (5) Technoprobe's raised guide caps the upside. Result: fair value $130 (from $136), scenario mean about $143, and a 12-month median of about $137 (from $140) against the actual $149.15 close. The ladder is lognormal-like with sigma about 0.62: below the 85% realized vol because part of that came from re-rating jumps, with the left tail fattened for the cyclical-crash base rate. Kalshi's 2027 recession market (about 22c) is unchanged. I discounted the generic doubling and big-year studies flagged by the supervisor and no longer lean on them. No option data was used, and nothing under priors/ was opened. Research this round was limited to EDGAR plus two searches for historical EPS.
